newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-CARSON ALL SET TO RETIRE AFTER CLASSICS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CARSON ALL SET TO RETIRE AFTER CLASSICS.

text.p: Veteran Willie Carson, who has won the Epsom Derby four times, is all set to retire this year after completing his comeback from life-threatening injury, it was reported on Monday.
Carson, 54, aims to return to action this spring but sees himself joining long-time rival Lester Piggott in retirement in 1997.
"Most of the classics come in the early part of the season. Once they are over, I will take a view as to my future," the Scot told the Daily Mail.
"Lester was falling off horses by the end. He went on far too long. I can't see any further than this year for myself."
Carson has been out of action since a bad accident at Newbury last September when he was kicked in the paddock by an unraced horse.
He spent a week and a half in hospital with severe liver injuries which led many to forecast his imminent retirement.
But the five-times champion jockey aims to return to the saddle in time to partner ante-post favourite Bahhare in the 2000 Guineas at Newmarket in May and has already got back on a horse.
"I had no problem getting back on a horse, it's just like riding a bicycle," Carson said.
